reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 10 close: SPX 7,520.93, -4.13% from its 120-day high and -1.98% below its 50-day but +2.59% above its 200-day; SMH 483.63 inside Zone 2 ($470-505), -28.0% from its high; NVDA 168.89 below the $175 Zone 2 floor, voiding the Nov 9 suspected bottom; VIX 19.46 rolling over from a 28.18 five-day high; HY OAS 3.34 calm; mechanical tally 3 of 4. Midday Nov 11 is bouncing hard (QQQ +2.97%, TQQQ +8.91%) but the bounce has not closed.
reaction.invalidation: SPX closes above 7,820 with SMH above 600 and VIX holding below 17 — the correction is over, the Watch stance was too cautious, and the ladder's trap framing is void. Conversely, SPX closing below the 200-day at 7,331.08 proves the correction is deepening into a regime break and voids the Tranche A re-arm path entirely.

ladder.trigger: NVDA closes back inside Zone 2 ($175-185) AND SMH closes holding Zone 2 ($470-505) with VIX below 25 and the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better

ladder.response: Treat as the bull trap: do not chase the bounce, cut any probe entered on it, stay in Watch with cash
ladder.trigger: SPX closes into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone or SMH into 580-600, then rolls over and closes back below the zone

ladder.response: Tranche A stays void; no probe at the next leg down until zones are re-mapped — the correction is escalating, not bottoming
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below the $470 Zone 2 floor, or NVDA closes below $168.89 (the Nov 10 low close)

ladder.response: Stand down: regime-break conditions met, Tranche A re-arm is off the table and the ladder is suspended pending a fresh regime read

ladder.response: Confirmed-bottom conditions for Tranche C: re-audit zones and ratios before deploying the 50% tranche — no auto-deployment

reaction.trapRisk: Today's bounce is exactly the pivot-and-fail shape: TQQQ +8.91% and NVDA +4.89% intraday, NVDA only just back above $175 live after the Nov 9 suspected bottom was voided by a close below that same line. Do not chase the first bounce and do not size on intraday prices — entries wait for a close back inside Zone 2, and any probe taken on the bounce is cut if SPX rejects the 7,750-7,820 failure zone.

strategyPosture: Watch. The midday bounce is sharp — QQQ +2.97%, VIX down 10.95% to 17.33 — but it is intraday and unconfirmed: NVDA only reclaimed $175 live after closing below it, and the correction's failure zone (SPX 7,750-7,820) sits above. Hold cash; no probe until a close confirms.

themes.counterRead: The divergence itself is the risk: concentration this wide means the index can look fine while the names that drove it keep falling. If credit flips — HY OAS above 4% or lending standards tightening — the rotation read dies and the rollover read takes over. Until then, index-level calm is real, not a mask.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY is only 2.50% below its 52-week high against the Mag 7 average of -15.49%, a 12.99-point divergence gap; GOOGL is the weakest Mag 7 name at -27.8% while AAPL is -0.1%. Credit is not confirming a rollover: bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.34, calm. The index is rotating leadership, not breaking.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover — At Its Hardest Test
themes.narrative: The tape reads like an AI unwind becoming a broad rollover: the Mag 7 sit on average 15.49% below their 52-week highs while the index holds near its own.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4% or SLOOS moving toward the stress zone; Mag 7 average distance from highs narrowing back under 10 points.

themes.counterRead: Revenue growth this strong against prices 27-44% below highs is the classic DATA_AHEAD setup, but NVDA's decline is classified ACUTE_CATALYST, not sentiment — the catalyst behind the 'Nvidia in the hot seat' headline is unresolved, and it is why the Nov 9 bottom failed. The bounce is a test, not a confirmation: a close back inside Zone 2 re-arms the probe; a rejection at the SPX failure zone (7,750-7,820) confirms the trap.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals moved the other way while prices fell: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY, AVGO 55%, ONTO 41.5%, and DDOG 27.7%. NVDA closed Nov 10 at $168.89, below the $175 floor, with RSI 31.4; SMH closed at $483.63, inside Zone 2 ($470-505). Midday Nov 11 the complex is bouncing hard — NVDA live $176.76 (+4.89%), TQQQ +8.91%, VRT +8.65% — but NVDA has only reclaimed $175 intraday, not on a close.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure: The Bounce Into the Failure Zone
themes.narrative: The market believes the AI buildout trade is broken: NVDA is 22.52% lower over one month and SMH is 28.01% off its high, and the Nov 9 suspected bottom was voided when NVDA closed below the $175 Zone 2 floor.
themes.watchFor: NVDA close vs the $175 Zone 2 floor; SMH close vs the $470 Zone 2 floor; SPX close vs the 7,750-7,820 failure zone.

themes.counterRead: Insider buying at the trough against a 28.5% drawdown is the strongest fundamental-vs-price gap in the book, and it is why VST carries the only conviction promotion. The open question is entry quality, not thesis: the name has to prove it can hold the bounce before it earns size.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is the conviction promotion (score 83) at $135.33, -28.5% from its peak, with insiders buying $1.17M at the trough, revenue growing 19.1% YoY, positive free cash flow of $1,318M, and a 2.6x price-to-sales ratio. The whole complex is bouncing midday — VST +3.22%, OKLO +5.04%, CCJ +2.96% — off the same trough. VST reported Nov 6 and has no earnings before Jan 13, 2027.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power: Insider Buying Into the Trough
themes.narrative: Power names are being sold as AI collateral damage: CCJ is -12.91% over one month, OKLO -17.07%, SMR -18.33%, GEV -18.48%.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above $135.33 into the close; any follow-through insider buying.

themes.counterRead: This is the widest fundamentals-vs-price gap in the universe: platform-level margins and 27-34% revenue growth against 37-65% drawdowns. But every one of these declines is tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not a single-stock catalyst — the market is de-rating the whole cohort at once, and cohort de-ratings do not reverse on one good print. DDOG is the cleanest test case because its numbers are the strongest and its next earnings are two months out.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is the top conviction name (score 82, tier A) at $187.91, -37.5% from its high with RSI 33.3, revenue growing 27.7% YoY, 80% gross margin, and $1,001M of free cash flow at a 29.2% margin; it reported Nov 4 and has no earnings before Jan 13, 2027. NOW sits at RSI 31.2 with a -25.8% one-month trend. TTD is already bouncing, +32.3% over one month.
themes.label: Software / SaaS: Growth Intact, Prices Halved

themes.watchFor: DDOG holding its bounce with RSI lifting out of the low-30s; NOW stabilizing above $102.92 after a -25.8% month.

themes.counterRead: Rates and credit agree with each other — higher-for-longer pricing without stress — which is why this theme is ALIGNED rather than a warning. The break condition is specific: if the Dec FOMC repricing pushes the 10-year toward the 5.2% falsifier line while HY OAS breaks 4%, the rates story stops being a rotation headwind and becomes the regime break. Until then it is a headwind the tape is already carrying.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year sits at 4.88% with the real 10-year at 2.68% and the 2s10s curve at +0.32, uninverted and steepening; the 2-year is 4.56% against a 3.88% policy rate, and breakeven inflation (T10IE) is 2.20%. Credit is not cracking alongside the repricing: HY OAS 3.34 and SLOOS loose at 1.7%.
themes.label: Rates Repricing After Hot CPI
themes.narrative: Hot October CPI killed rate-cut hopes and the market is repricing toward hikes: the FOMC decision Dec 8-9 and the Nov 18 minutes are now the gates, with PCE Oct on Nov 25 in between.
themes.watchFor: 10-year vs the 5.2% falsifier line; HY OAS vs 4%; FOMC minutes Nov 18 for any shift in the Dec 8-9 path.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move is decided at two lines: NVDA's $175 Zone 2 floor and the SPX 7,750-7,820 failure zone. A NVDA close back inside Zone 2 with SMH holding $470 re-arms the Tranche A probe; a bounce that stalls and rolls over at the failure zone confirms the trap and keeps the ladder on the sidelines.
